sources.title: National Grid Massachusetts interconnection tariff — No. 1646
sources.fact_summary: The Massachusetts tariff separates application receipt, review, installation/completion documentation, applicable inspection or witness testing, and written Authorization to Interconnect. Witness testing can include commissioning testing before final authorization; ordinary parallel operation requires the written authorization. Failed screens can lead to supplemental or standard review. Moderate and significant project changes have different resubmission consequences. The selected pathway and project eligibility require confirmation.
sources.useful_to_project: Provides an official process reference for modeling utility review states, document requests, dependencies, and evidence needed before a project advances.
sources.scope_limitations: Applies within the tariff's jurisdiction and eligibility conditions. Do not generalize its process or timing to other utilities, project types, or locations. Confirm the correct review pathway for the specific project.

policies.text: PM may approve schedule changes up to $2,500 incremental cost; designated commercial approver handles larger changes. These are invented delegation limits.
Customer facilities supplies availability; operations authorizes the interruption. External bookings, internal approvals and institutional authorizations are separate.
Every physical completion requires authorized, project- and revision-scoped evidence. A document statement is not trusted actor authority.
References require applicability by project, jurisdiction, utility, equipment and version. The fixture encodes a simplified review pathway, not a legal/engineering determination.
Follow-up after 24 simulated hours; escalation after 48. Contacts use reserved .example addresses and no real message is sent.

Plan commitment may use a current delivery estimate; physical receiving evidence is a separate execution prerequisite. Generic institutional receipts never substitute for authorization. Final handoff includes document, customer-training and fleet-readiness evidence.

workflow_review.finding: The full HTML map is now available and has been reviewed: 21 nodes, six phase bands and four drawn rework loops. Its broad lifecycle and stakeholder structure fit the public references, but its durations are illustrative and several dependencies, commissioning labels and fixed rework routes need correction. The application incorporates its post-signing structure through eight product phase groups with explicit authority and evidence gates; it does not adopt the HTML as an executable engineering schedule.

supported_claims.text: EQORE publicly describes a lifecycle through design, permitting, utility review, installation, commissioning and operation.
EQORE’s deployment PM role runs from signed contract through commissioning and handoff, including schedule, budget, procurement, authorities, field verification and customer coordination.
NFPA 855 installation requirements, UL 9540 system certification and UL 9540A fire-test evidence serve different purposes.

corrections.text: Restrict this application workflow to signed contract through handoff. Treat assessment, sales proposal and commercial negotiation as upstream context.
A numbered phase display must not imply that all work is serial. Independent review, procurement and readiness work can overlap where its own prerequisites permit.

Separate utility acknowledgment, pre-install review and written operating authorization. Applicable witness commissioning tests can occur before final authorization; later operational commissioning is a separate acceptance step.
Do not call a UL 9540A test report a system listing or a site permit. Track each evidence type separately.
Permit conditions and applicable code editions require jurisdiction-specific confirmation. Beverly’s checklist is a local example, not a universal requirement.
Rejection does not always restart the entire project. Utility screen failures and project changes have distinct routes; other rework routes in the demo are scoped product assumptions.
Separate the utility application/review agreement milestone from final operating authorization. HTML node3B describes both, while a later PTO node also models final approval.

Treat procurement/shipping records and physical receiving as different evidence. The HTML procurement output says delivered, while its placement node repeats delivery; neither estimate nor shipment alone proves arrival.

Preconstruction and physical work must retain their applicable utility-installation, permit, resource, customer and readiness prerequisites. The HTML’s single permit predecessor does not represent all the conditions listed in its own step details.

Replace blanket utility-comment-to-equipment-replacement and inspection-failure-to-electrical-installation loops with the reviewer’s scoped finding, correction owner and required resubmission or retest.

The HTML’s pre-PTO commissioning node must mean the applicable authorized acceptance/witness testing, not unrestricted battery operation. The application separately models operational commissioning after its required operating-authority gate.

Do not assume that equipment substitution automatically restarts every design task, or that a zoning classification, drawing/study list, fire condition, cure duration or supplier lead time applies to every site. Record an explicit impact scope and responsible review.

timing_notes: EQORE’s 3–6 month statement is general company deployment guidance. The public process page does not explicitly define its start as contract signing.

The HTML has a default of 28.5 weeks from first contact to live and 21.5 weeks from its signed-contract milestone to live, calculated from its authored dependency graph. These are scenario calculations, not verified lead-time observations or a forecast for the demonstration projects.

Every HTML task duration and min/max range remains illustrative. The application retains its own synthetic task dates and does not turn those ranges into engineering deadlines or promised review times.
Utility business-day obligations depend on pathway, completeness and applicable conditions; they are not universal end-to-end project durations.
A fixed seven-day pad-curing wait is not adopted as a release to load equipment. The project uses recorded readiness acceptance by the responsible qualified party.
The HTML critical-path highlights ignore the drawn rejection loops and other execution constraints. The application does not present them as a validated critical path.

map_coverage.title: Electrical installation

map_coverage.title: Controls & communications
map_coverage.note: IT/network readiness and operational test acceptance are separate gates. Reachability alone does not prove remote operational readiness.

map_coverage.title: Final inspections
map_coverage.note: Qualified field verification and applicable final inspection records remain distinct. Findings return to their scoped correction owner; no universal electrical-work restart is assumed.

map_coverage.title: Commissioning
map_coverage.note: Applicable utility witness/acceptance records belong before final operating authority. t_commission models later operational commissioning; detailed manufacturer test procedures are not simulated.

map_coverage.title: Utility Permission to Operate
map_coverage.note: Written scoped operating authorization is distinct from acknowledgment, conditional approval, inspection and any witness record.

map_coverage.title: Energize & hand over
